jobs.description: Employer: Man Group Expires: 11/10/2026 The TeamMan Systematics’ Fast Trading Strategies (FTS) team is responsible for the development of high Sharpe, high-frequency trading strategies across all asset classes. The team has been running for over a decade and currently manages a large and successful portfolio across both global futures and cash markets. The FTS team is responsible for the full end to end development of the fast alpha portfolio, using several techniques to capture fast alphas, ML, event driven, microstructure based etc, building its own customized monetization stack, and optimizing trading and order placement with dedicated high-frequency infrastructure.This posting is specifically for candidates interested in interning in the New York office, which houses Man Systematics’ business unit focused on high-frequency alpha research, trading, and infrastructure.Who Should Apply?The team is currently hiring PhD students for an MLE/QR internship with strong academic achievement in highly technical degree programs who are interested in a summer internship (expected to be between 10 – 12 weeks).Candidates are encouraged to submit only one application using their university email address via the below link, which requires a resume that includes all completed and in-progress post-secondary education GPAs. School transcripts may be optionally provided immediately or later in the process.Kindly note that our summer internships are open to penultimate year students only.Purpose of the RoleThe MLE role is ideal for individuals who are passionate about software that is focused on machine learning applications such as MLOps and research workflows. Because MLEs are also expected to use their own software, the ideal candidate not only has experience coding in a variety of languages (especially Python) but also has knowledge of ML algorithms and research processes.The QR role is ideal for individuals who are passionate about using high frequency tick data and machine learning algorithms to predict asset returns and converting those models into profitable trading strategies. QRs will work closely with MLOps in deploying models and therefore are required to be strong programmers in a variety of languages (especially Python). Previous ML or statistical research internship experience in finance, technology, or academia is strongly preferred.Working HereMan Systematic fosters a performance driven, meritocratic culture with a small company, no-attitude feel. It is flat structured, open, transparent, and collaborative, offering ample opportunity to grow and have enormous impact on what we do. We are actively engaged with the broader research and academic community, as well as renowned industry contributors.We’re fortunate enough to have a modern high-rise office in central Midtown conveniently located near Central Park and continually strive to make our environment a great place in which to work.We have annual away days and research off-sites for the whole team.We open-source some of our technology. See https://github.com/man-groupWe regularly talk at leading industry conferences, and tweet about relevant technology and how we’re using it. See @manquanttech and @ManGroup.Our Oxford lab is collocated with the Oxford-Man Institute of Quantitative Finance (https://bit.ly/36goTic) and the Machine Learning Research Group in Engineering Science, University of Oxford (https://bit.ly/2MSHDwy)

jobs.description: Employer: GlobalFoundries Expires: 11/10/2026 About GlobalFoundriesGlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, powe-refficient and high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. GF is a trusted and holistic technology partner for customers around the world. GF’s talented, global team remains focused every day on security, longevity and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com. Internship Program Overview: Our Interns & Co-ops are our entry-level talent pipeline for GF across the globe. Our goal is to provide students with a meaningful work experience that will equip them with the skills to embark on a career in the fast-paced and growing semiconductor industry after graduation. As an intern at GF, you’ll experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives. Summary of Role:The CMOS BEOL Reliability Engineering Intern will support the Fab 8 Reliability Engineering organization in developing and implementing an inline methodology to assess risks associated with critical back-end-of-line defects in automotive products. Working with Reliability Engineering, Contamination-Free Manufacturing, and Process Integration teams, the intern will connect manufacturing defect data and reliability physics to develop product-relevant defective-parts-per-million risk metrics and actionable monitoring insights. Essential Responsibilities include:Learn the fundamentals of BEOL reliability, semiconductor failure mechanisms, inline defect monitoring, reliability risk assessment, and Failure Modes and Effects Analysis.Analyze inline defect data and scanning electron microscope images to identify and evaluate manufacturing defects that may affect product reliability.Connect observed defect types with potential BEOL degradation mechanisms, including electromigration and time-dependent dielectric breakdown, to assess reliability criticality.Perform statistical analysis to understand key risk drivers and help translate normalized defect density into product-relevant defective-parts-per-million risk estimates.Develop data-analysis and visualization tools or dashboards that communicate defect trends, calculated risk, assumptions, and sensitivity to key inputs.Support development of consistent monitoring methodologies for reliability-critical defects in representative automotive products.Collaborate with Reliability Engineering, Contamination-Free Manufacturing, and Process Integration teams; document methods and results; and communicate project status through reports and presentations.Develop a documented defect catalog linking selected inline defect types to their potential BEOL reliability impact and applicable degradation mechanisms.Deliver a final technical presentation summarizing the inline reliability risk-assessment method, results, limitations, and recommendations for implementation or follow-on work. Other Responsibilities:Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs. Required Qualifications:Education – At least a sophomore at time of application and actively pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Semiconductor Engineering, or related field through an accredited degree program during the time of internship.Must have at least an overall 3.0 GPA and be in good academic standing.Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal)Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship.Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills.Ability to work independently while collaborating in a cross-functional engineering environment. Preferred Qualifications: Prior related internship or co-op experienceDemonstrated prior leadership experience in the workplace, school projects, competitions, etc.Strong interest in leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to enhance productivity, streamline workflows, and support effective decision-making.Project management skills, i.e., the ability to innovate and execute on solutions that matter; the ability to navigate ambiguity.Strong written and verbal communication skillsStrong planning & organizational skillsCoursework or experience in semiconductor devices, materials, manufacturing, reliability, statistics, or data analytics.Familiarity with BEOL interconnects, copper metallization, dielectric materials, defect mechanisms, electromigration, or time-dependent dielectric breakdown.Experience with Python, JMP, Minitab, Excel, Power BI, MATLAB, or similar analysis and visualization tools.Experience organizing technical data, automating calculations, developing dashboards, or presenting engineering results.#InternshipProgramUS Expected Salary Range$20.00 - $40.00 The exact Salary will be determined based on qualifications, experience and location. This role also collaborates with internal teams and vendors to meet project timelines and objectives, promoting operational excellence across all aspects of the project lifecycle, including compliance with industry standards, lean principles, and best practices. however, all qualified candidates will be considered regardless of their current clearance status. The ability to obtain and maintain a Department of Energy security clearance is required.Preferred Job Requirements:Minimum GPA of 3.0 is preferred.Working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint. Outlook, etc.) and other commonly used business applications or role specific applications.Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills - including effective technical writing skills.Able to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment, with strong attention to detail and deadlines. Committed to maintaining high standards of quality.Demonstrated ability to build and maintain positive working relationships, both internally and externally.Ability to adapt to evolving project requirements while maintaining compliance with organizational policies, procedures, and applicable regulations. Ability to follow a structured project management process including document meeting minutes, action items, and monitor progress. Capability and tenacity for solving unique engineering problems. Ability to learn quickly and a desire to keep improving skills and to teach others when possible. Team player with a highly proactive and positive attitude with ability to work on own or in a team as needed. Hands-on skills. Demonstrated interest in building and testing. Regular, predictable attendance is required. Please note that estimated time for start/end dates are based on Spring 2027. Other semesters will have different dates. Want to know more about each of our Area Assignments? Let our managers tell you! Conversion Engineering: The Conversion Engineering Team is responsible for controller-generators and starter-generators (as well as converting the power they produce). We design and support multiple products with our current new product introduction (NPI) programs. The Mechanical Engineering Team designs the housings and assembly methods for our systems, ensuring they meet strict environmental and operational requirements. Their work is essential to delivering robust and reliable solutions for our aerospace applications. Embedded Systems Engineering: If you're curious about how hardware and software come together to power real-world systems and are eager to make an impact while learning from experienced engineers - join our Embedded Systems Engineering team. Industrialization Engineering: Industrialization is the perfect blend of design and manufacturing work. We have a mix of both in reviewing engineering drawings, discussing design features, developing solutions, mitigating design risks, managing prototype builds, building tooling, and implementing new products into production. We get the benefit of working with every department in the business and every day is different. If you want to have a mix of design work behind a desk and time on the production floor seeing designs you helped create come to life - then Industrialization is right for you! Manufacturing Engineering: As a Co-Op, you will work directly with our production team and design engineers to support the assembly and troubleshooting of aircrafts power-conversion units. We perform root-cause analysis on units that fail functional testing, remove roadblocks for our production team, diagnose defective parts, improve assembly processes, update work instructions, and initiate corrective actions. If you want hands-on experience on the shop floor and to improve efficiency while reducing waste - apply for Manufacturing Engineering. Production Support Engineering: Working in Production Support Engineering you will have the opportunity to work on real products and support day-to-day engineering activities that directly impact production, product reliability, and customer satisfaction. Responsibilities may include assisting with failure investigations, supporting resolution of production and supplier-related issues, evaluating nonconforming hardware, participating in repair and overhaul activities, reviewing engineering documentation, and contributing to engineering changes that improve product performance, manufacturability, and long-term supportability. Project Management: Everything starts with an idea, and project managers bring ideas into reality. From managing and executing plans, creative problem solving, and balancing the needs and expectations of a cross-functional team; project managers touch every aspect of the business and the world around us. With Project Management at Safran you will get real world understanding of how products and projects come to life, leveraging the strength of the team and how to manage risks and budget along the way. Quality Engineering: If you're looking to help ensure customer satisfaction and promote continual improvement of our products and processes, then the Quality Team may be for you. Our team is responsible for maintaining our Quality Management System (QMS), facilitating Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), and conducting internal quality audits. We promote continual improvement in the form of corrective actions and improvement projects. Rotating Machines Engineering: The mechanical design team within the Rotating Machines Department excels in engineering robust and high-performance aircraft rotating machinery. This includes generators and starter-generator systems. This group specializes in designing critical mechanical components such as rotors, stators, shafts, bearings, splines, and housings to ensure reliability and efficiency under demanding aerospace conditions. Supply Chain Engineering: Supply Chain is where ideas are transformed into finished products. We partner closely with suppliers to secure everything the business requires—from engineering components to the materials, equipment, and services that support daily operations. You'll gain firsthand experience in turning plans into reality by collaborating with suppliers, resolving challenges, and ensuring materials flow efficiently throughout the process. Systems/ Analysis Engineering: The System Integration & Performance Team develops, integrates, and validates aerospace electrical power systems by bringing together hardware, software, and control systems into a complete solution. Team members support system testing, performance analysis, troubleshooting, and certification activities to ensure products meet customer and regulatory requirements. Test Engineering: The Test Engineering Team specializes in test design, execution, and reporting for all power units. The team is composed of both test engineers and test equipment engineers. The test engineers handle the design, setup, execution, reporting of research and development testing, and qualification testing of new products and/or systems. Meanwhile, the test equipment engineering team design mechanical, electrical, and control equipment for the test lab to enable both production and new product testing to take place. Through Life Support Engineering: The Through Life Support Engineering team works on the problems that happen after designs enter production. The team investigates failures (both in the field and on the production line), solves production and supplier issues, supports repair and overhaul activity, evaluates nonconforming hardware, manages obsolescence, and develops design and drawing changes that keep products operating safely and reliably throughout their service life. For Co-Ops, it is a great opportunity to work on real hardware, see how engineering decisions affect the entire product lifecycle, and gain hands-on experience through a wide variety of technical challenges compared to working on a piece of a long-term development program.

program visibility across the security organization.Qualifications• Pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Engineering Management, Cybersecurity, or a related field.• platforms.• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously.• Nice to Have: Exposure to PPM or work management tools (e.g., ServiceNow, jobs.title: Fundraising and Development Intern at Gilda’s Club Grand Rapids and Gilda’s LaughFest
jobs.description: Employer: Gilda’s Club Grand Rapids and Gilda’s LaughFest Expires: 11/12/2026 Gilda’s Club Grand Rapids is seeking Fundraising and Development Interns. Join a seasoned Vice President of Fund Development and participate in hands on experiences that will enhance your studies. Fundraising and development interns are responsible for assisting with the organization’s overall fundraising strategy and goals for special events. Internships can be further tailored to fit the student’s goals and objectives. Our team at Gilda’s Club can provide learning opportunities for donor solicitation (individual and corporate), event management, and communications. Gilda's Club Grand Rapids is a free emotional health support community of children, adults, families, and friends on any kind of cancer journey or those grieving a death due to any cause. Its comprehensive program, delivered by professionals, includes education, structured sharing times, networking, lectures, workshops, and social activities. For more information, visit gildasclubgr.org. This is an unpaid internship; however, a $500 stipend can be provided upon successful completion. We work with the intern to best establish a schedule that is mutually beneficial. Experience may count toward school credit. This internship is set up to support three areas: Event Management- Gilda’s Club hosts its annual LaughFest and Red Door Gala in March. Be a part of the planning for this extra special community event that will celebrate free cancer and grief support. Key components of this work will include data management, solicit area businesses and provide logistical support and leadership oversight of event volunteers. Communications- Gilda’s Club and Gilda’s LaughFest have many communication touch points for event attendees. Interns will provide support in this process through database management, helping to ensure all donors are coded correctly for receiving communication, and development of useful content for the E-newsletters and letters. Data Analyzes- The final piece of this internship will include working on data analyzes to help Gilda’s Club understand and study the ROI for the year-end campaign. This project will be in conjunction with the VP of Development and will be made into a presentation to share with our Fund Development sub-committee of the Board of Directors. RequirementsEnrolled in an accredited college or universityOrganized and detail orientedExcellent ability to communicate in person, print and electronically to variable audiencesAbility to manage multiple projects simultaneouslyHigh level of integrity, diplomacy, and initiativeProficiency with Microsoft Office applications (especially Word & Excel)Complete work during normal business hours (between 8:30AM-6:00PM) with flexibility to assist on occasional evenings/weekends Applicants, please email Résumé and Cover Letter to Shawn Campbell, VP of Development, scampbell@gildasclubgr.org

jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 11/14/2026 Reference Code USAMRDC-MRIID-2026-0008RHow to ApplyAll applications must be submitted through Zintellect at www.zintellect.comDescriptionThe Department of Defense (DoD) is offering a postdoctoral fellowship at the U.S. Army Medical Research and Development Command – Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases (USAMRDC MRIID).What will I be doing? As an Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) participant, you will engage in efforts to advance translational antiviral drug discovery. Research activities will include recombinant protein expression and purification, biochemical screening assay development, computational structural modeling, cell-based antiviral validation studies, and exposure to preclinical small-animal research models.Why Should I Apply? Under the guidance of a mentor, you will engage in research activities that include, but are not limited to: Designing, expressing, purifying, and characterizing recombinant viral and host proteins to support biochemical and structural studies. Applying computational tools to analyze protein structure and function, identify potential binding pockets, and map small-molecule interactions. Developing and using biochemical and cell-based assays to evaluate candidate antiviral compounds and investigate their mechanisms of action. Gaining experience with high-throughput phenotypic drug screening and anti-viral assays and applying promising therapeutic candidates in organoid and zebrafish disease models, with opportunities to support subsequent preclinical small-animal studies. Learning research that integrates protein science, computational analysis, and antiviral drug discovery with advanced disease models, including organoids and zebrafish, to evaluate promising therapeutic candidates. Where will I be located? Frederick, Maryland What is the anticipated start date? The USAMRIID is ready to make appointments immediately. Exact start dates will be determined at the time of selection and in coordination with the selected candidate. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis and internships or fellowships will be filled as qualified candidates are identified. What is the appointment length? Appointments are initially for one year with the option to extend the appointment for up to four additional years, contingent upon project needs and funding availability. What are the provisions? You will receive a stipend to be determined by MRIID. The stipend range for this opportunity is $70,000-$80,000/12-month appointment. Stipends are typically based on a participant’s academic standing, discipline, experience, and research facility location. Other provisions may include the following: • Health Insurance Supplement (Participants are eligible to purchase health insurance through ORISE) • Relocation Allowance • Training and Travel Allowance Security Clearance While participants will not enter an employment relationship with DoD or any other agency, this opportunity will require a suitability investigation/background investigation. Any offer made is considered tentative pending favorable outcome of the investigation.

jobs.title: 2027 Monarch Quantum Summer Internship Program at Monarch Quantum
jobs.description: Employer: Monarch Quantum Expires: 11/14/2026 The Monarch Quantum Summer Internship Program offers students the opportunity to work on cutting‑edge technology shaping the future of quantum computing. Interns join multidisciplinary teams and contribute to real engineering projects that support our quantum hardware, software, and system‑level development efforts.As a Monarch intern, you may help design or test components, build experimental setups, develop control or automation software, analyze system performance, or support integration of quantum‑safe technologies—depending on your background and interests. Interns collaborate closely with experienced engineers and researchers while gaining hands‑on experience in a fast‑moving, industry‑focused environment.We encourage applications from students who are curious, motivated, and excited to apply their technical skills to emerging quantum technologies. Opportunities are available for students at the bachelor's, master’s and PhD levels.Some project examples include:Develop a test fixture for assessing the stability of opto-mechanical bonds & assemblies and perform stability experiments. The intern will define test goals & requirements, execute mechanical & optical design of a fixture and test station, facilitate material procurement, build the assembly, execute testing, compile results, and deliver a presentation to engineering leadership. The intern will also participate in ongoing projects to gain exposure in a professional, high precision engineering environment.Work hands-on with an optically pumped semiconductor laser (OPSL) system in an ISO-7 (Class 10,000) cleanroom laboratory, collaborating with and mentored by junior and senior engineers as well as senior management. Intern project opportunities in this role include, but are not limited to, material characterization; device-level semiconductor laser characterization such as spectral analysis and power-efficiency measurements; and optical and thermal modeling using tools such as Zemax, COMSOL, SolidWorks, and ANSYS. Interns will gain practical experience across the full development cycle, from simulation and design through laboratory testing and analysis.Contribute to the optical design of components and lenses for next‑generation laser modules. Interns will help develop and design test stations used to evaluate both individual components and full module assemblies. The role includes hands‑on intern involvement in building and operating these test stations to collect and analyze performance data. The intern will also support the development and validation of new design methodologies for laser module engineeringSupport the development of advanced automated pick‑and‑place routines for a fully integrated robotic cell consisting of multiple 6‑DOF industrial robots. The project includes designing, implementing, and testing motion control algorithms that improve accuracy, speed, and reliability of component handling within the automated cell. The intern will collaborate with robotics engineers to develop end‑to‑end workflows, including path planning, error detection, sensor integration, and automation sequencing. In addition, the intern will help evaluate system performance, optimize cycle times, and contribute to documentation and validation of the robotic software stack.Design a reliability test station for cutting-edge photonics components. Develop requirements, procure parts, and build a test system that allows a laser to auto-focus into a micron-sized target. Interns will utilize CAD software to design the test layout and work directly to set up the experiment in a cleanroom laser laboratory environment. They will write a script in python or LabView to perform the auto-focusing calibration routine.Work alongside experienced engineers to design, analyze, document, and test electrical systems and prototypes. Intern responsibilities include schematic development, PCB documentation, data analysis, test execution, and supporting failure analysis and corrective actions. This project provides extensive opportunities for technical skill-building, mentorship, and exposure to professional electrical engineering practices.Support the build and test of existing and novel External Cavity Diode Laser (ECDL) products through hands on lab experiments. Interns will join the laser development team and will design and execute tests to prove components and full laser assemblies to support Monarch Quantum's mission to deliver high-quality light engines to our customers. Project opportunities include building and characterizing laser cavities with novel components, designing diode test stations, improving alignment processes, and modeling laser systems. Interns will be mentored by collaborating with senior scientists, management, and laser technicians. Interns will leave the experience with a strong theoretical knowledge of and hands-on experience with ECDLs.Focus on developing FPGA-based systems using hybrid C/C++ and HDL architectures, including designing interfaces to ADCs, DACs, microcontrollers, and other components. Interns will support the creation and testing of advanced data acquisition and analysis systems, participate in hardware‑firmware integration, and contribute to reviews, verification, and documentation.Support the development of automated optical assembly processes, with a focus on investigating adhesive properties and performance when bonding precision optics to metal components. Interns will design and execute experiments to characterize adhesive behavior, develop and refine process parameters, and evaluate the impact on optical performance and assembly quality. They will also receive hands-on training in optical alignment, precision motion systems, and robotic automation. This project will provide practical experience at the intersection of optics, materials, process development, and robotics.
